doc:
UI-ready inline-hint bundle for the close-position amount/price inputs.

Retires the three Kotlin local computations in
`RustClosePositionBottomSheet.kt`:
- `:251` `TradeInputUtils.getPriceTickSizeMsg(price, instTitle, instType)`
→ [`price_tick_msg`]
- `:302` `TradeInputUtils.getAmtTickSizeMsg(amt, instTitle, instType)`
→ [`amount_tick_msg`]
- `:312` `TradeInputUtils.getProbablyValue(price, amt, instTitle, instType,
indexPrice)` → [`probably_value`]

Produced by `ClosePositionManager::build_input_validation(price, amount)`
and projected into `OKTClosePositionState.input_validation`. The Kotlin
listeners read these fields directly instead of calling `TradeInputUtils`
/ `OKTNumberF` locally.

# Per-instType coverage (A6 sibling fan-out)
- `price_tick_msg` is produced for **every** instType that exposes a
`tick_sz` (SWAP/FUTURES/MARGIN/OPTION/EVENT) via the shared
`GetBestPriceUseCase` (the verified `getPriceTickSizeMsg` port already
used by `increase_positions`).
- `amount_tick_msg` reuses `GetBestAmtUseCase` (`new_contract` for
SWAP/FUTURES, `new_option` for OPTION, `new_spot_or_margin` for
MARGIN/SPOT) plus the contract `check_contract_min_size_by_inst`
(SWAP/FUTURES only — it returns `Ok` and contributes no hint for other
inst types, matching Kotlin which gates min-size on contract biz).
- `probably_value` is produced for SWAP/FUTURES (`calculate_amount_pop`)
and OPTION (`calculate_estimated_value_use_case`). **MARGIN / SPOT /
EVENT probably-value convention is NOT ported** — the native
`getProbablyValue` branches for those biz lines live in the binary-only
`TradeInputUtils` that is not source-readable in this worktree, so the
value stays `None` there rather than fabricating a formula. See the
`R-MIG-TODO` note in `build_input_validation`.
